proof:
Source: parent proof, step 6 (|γ| ≡ 1 gives ⟨γ, γ′⟩ = 0; differentiating f(γ(α)) = α gives ⟨Aγ, γ′⟩ = |πγ|², so γ′ ≠ 0), stated for an arbitrary curve; orthonormality of u, e is not needed. Notation: I := (−s, s); ⟨·,·⟩ is the real inner product; γ′(α) := deriv γ α.
1. (Differentiability.) Fix α ∈ I. I is open, hence a neighbourhood of α. ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ I gives DifferentiableOn ℝ γ I (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≠ 0), so γ is differentiable at α and HasDerivAt γ (γ′(α)) α.
2. (Orthogonality.) n(β) := ⟨γ(β), γ(β)⟩ = ‖γ(β)‖² equals 1 for all β ∈ I, a neighbourhood of α, so n has derivative 0 at α. By the product rule for inner products (HasDerivAt.inner), n has derivative ⟨γ′(α), γ(α)⟩ + ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 2⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ at α. By uniqueness of derivatives, ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 0.
3. (Derivative of the angle.) Let A(β) := ⟨γ(β), u⟩ and B(β) := ⟨γ(β), e⟩. By HasDerivAt.inner with a constant second argument they have derivatives A′ := ⟨γ′(α), u⟩ and B′ := ⟨γ′(α), e⟩ at α. Put x := A(α) > 0 and y := B(α). By the quotient rule (x ≠ 0), B/A has derivative (B′x − yA′)/x² at α, and by Real.hasDerivAt_arctan with the chain rule (HasDerivAt.arctan), h(β) := arctan(B(β)/A(β)) has derivative (1/(1 + (y/x)²))·(B′x − yA′)/x² = (B′x − yA′)/(x² + y²) at α, because (1 + (y/x)²)·x² = x² + y².
4. (Comparison.) By hypothesis h(β) = β for all β ∈ I, a neighbourhood of α, so h has derivative 1 at α (HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq with hasDerivAt_id). Hence (B′x − yA′)/(x² + y²) = 1, and since x² + y² ≥ x² > 0, xB′ − yA′ = x² + y², i.e. ⟨γ(α),u⟩⟨γ′(α),e⟩ − ⟨γ(α),e⟩⟨γ′(α),u⟩ = ⟨γ(α),u⟩² + ⟨γ(α),e⟩².
5. (Non-degeneracy.) The right-hand side in step 4 is ≥ x² > 0. If γ′(α) = 0, then A′ = B′ = 0 and the left-hand side would be 0. Hence γ′(α) ≠ 0. ∎
key_steps: γ is differentiable at every α ∈ (−s, s), being C¹ on an open interval.
Differentiating arctan(B/A) ≡ α with A = ⟨γ,u⟩ > 0, B = ⟨γ,e⟩ gives A⟨γ′,e⟩ − B⟨γ′,u⟩ = A² + B² > 0, hence γ′ ≠ 0.
